info.title: RstrBot HTTP API
info.description: Contract for actually registered release routes. All paths are absolute from the server origin. Current JSON success bodies use HTTP 200; documented no-content operations use 204. Browser authentication uses an HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie; non-browser callers may use the same opaque session token as Bearer (not a separately scoped API key). Authorization headers override cookies. Every API mutation without a Bearer-prefixed Authorization requires X-RstrBot-Request: 1, including setup/login. Cross-site Sec-Fetch-Site and mismatched Origin are rejected even with Bearer. No credentialed CORS is provided. The Google callback has its own single-use state/browser binding validation before exchanging a code. JSON bodies are limited to 1 MiB; UTF-8 byte limits are described with x-max-utf8-bytes. Unknown top-level fields are rejected only where the Rust request type declares deny_unknown_fields; generic data and ChatRequest are described separately. Examples are illustrative test data, not execution evidence. Unsupported capabilities have no invented endpoints.

x-contract-notes: Resource data schemas describe supported client configuration. Some serde_json::Value fields are intentionally permissive and may retain extra JSON; they are not claimed to be globally rejected.
All permission checks occur on the server against current membership/visibility; examples and schemas do not confer authority.
The path/method inventory covers explicitly registered handlers. Axum's implicit HEAD handling for GET routes does not create a separate business operation; OPTIONS/CORS support is not declared.
No API endpoint performs restore, executable installation, attachment upload, arbitrary sandbox execution, legacy compatibility or autonomous agent delegation in this release.
